dependencies.resolutionNote: Command/module resolution is intentionally not performed because discovery can import modules or run module initialization code.

findings.consequence: Publisher verification or command-collision protections may be disabled during dependency installation.
findings.remediation: Remove the bypass flag and install the pinned dependency into a private tool cache before importing its exact manifest path.

findings.message: String replacement appears to implement manual quote escaping.
findings.consequence: Hand-written escaping is context-sensitive and can permit injection when the result reaches code, command, SQL, LDAP, or another interpreter.
findings.remediation: Avoid constructing interpreter text. Use typed parameters or the target API parameterization mechanism.

findings.message: A catch block does not clearly report, rethrow, return, or terminate.
findings.consequence: Failures may be hidden and the script can continue in an invalid state.
findings.remediation: Handle the error explicitly, add useful context, and rethrow or return a documented failure result.

findings.message: State-changing command 'Install-Module' is not proven to be inside a same-scope ShouldProcess guard.
findings.consequence: The operation may run without a reliable -WhatIf preview or user confirmation boundary.
findings.remediation: Add [CmdletBinding(SupportsShouldProcess=$true)] to scope '<script>' and execute this command only inside if ($PSCmdlet.ShouldProcess(...)).

findings.message: 'Install-Module' does not pin an exact package version.
findings.consequence: A future or compromised package release can change script behaviour without a source-code change.
findings.remediation: Pin RequiredVersion/Version, constrain the repository, and record the loaded module path and hash.

findings.message: Formatting command 'Format-Table' is embedded in script logic.
findings.consequence: Formatting objects destroy structured pipeline data and make output difficult for agents and callers to consume reliably.
findings.remediation: Return normal objects or JSON from the analyzer logic and apply formatting only in an explicitly selected human-output mode.

testPlan.scenario: Parse every target under each declared PowerShell host
testPlan.expected: No parser errors and the same intended AST structure

testPlan.scenario: Exercise missing, null, malformed, boundary, and conflicting parameters
testPlan.expected: Deterministic validation errors with no side effects

testPlan.scenario: Force each external command and API call to fail
testPlan.expected: Non-zero/failed structured result; cleanup runs; no false success

testPlan.scenario: Run twice against the same prepared state
testPlan.expected: Second run is safe and converges without duplicate or destructive changes

testPlan.scenario: Use missing, locked, read-only, long, relative, traversal, and symlink/reparse-point paths
testPlan.expected: Targets remain inside the approved root and partial writes are cleaned up

limitations: Static analysis cannot prove runtime safety, intent, authorization, remote content, environment state, permissions, race behaviour, or all data flows.
Target scripts, modules, manifests, and tests were parsed/read only; none were imported, dot-sourced, invoked, or executed.
Command resolution is intentionally disabled because discovery can auto-import modules and run initialization code.
Malware assessment reports indicators, not a clean bill of health or a definitive malware classification.
Bounded decoders handle literal Base64 and gzip/deflate content; encrypted, custom-packed, runtime-built, or oversized payloads require an isolated specialist workflow.
